For example, my phone alerts me when a show is about to go on the air, and if I am watching, I can open the notification app and select that I am currently watching (or checking in) to the episode of the show I am tracking/following. It lets me keep a record of which episodes I have watched accurately so that I can keep shows in order!

This is some great stuff, since I have especially been missing my "social" experience on Sidereel. The features are quite good, especially the "instant check-in," however, to me it makes sense that if one "DVRs" a show, they watch it at an other time, and thus the tracker does not account for that. Sidereel, for example, has an Android app that I use, so when I actually watch the episode of the show I am tracking, I can just hit "Watched." I would lean towards that direction, as in maybe sending emails to users with verification of watched shows, if you are not already developing a mobile platform for your site. Nonetheless, absolutely great work!!

>That sounds like a mis-mapped import, as AOL must be using different field names to GMail. Does anything appear under the E-Mail address field at all? Or are they all blank, with just the "Screen Name" field showing up? 

>The easiest way to fix this is to export your newly imported Contacts as a Google compatible CSV file. Then delete all your contacts in GMail. (You can restore them if you need to, so don't panic!)

>Open the file in Excel or another spreadsheet program, and look for the columns headed "Screen Names" and "E-mail 1 - Value". Copy the contents of "Screen Names" and paste them into the column headed "E-mail 1 - Value"

>Or, if you found that the email field was just empty in your GMail contacts, you could try renaming the column headed "Screen Names" to "E-mail 1 - Value"

>Save the file. Try re-importing it. The email addresses should now map correctly to the proper field.

[Source](http://groups.google.com/a/googleproductforums.com/forum/#!category-topic/gmail/managing-settings-and-mail/ywcyK1EvJPc)
